title: Vocabulary List #1
extraNote: Removed from the list on 10/13. Study just in case.

words.tip: Adverse means "against you." Adversity is when life is working against you.
words.ex: Ryan showed courage in the face of {adversity} when he broke his arm right before the big game.
words.def: a difficult or unlucky situation; hardship

words.tip: ad + VOC (voice): an advocate adds their voice for someone else.
words.ex: She became an {advocate} for kids who needed safer bike lanes in the neighborhood.
words.def: to support a cause publicly; or a person who speaks up for others

words.tip: Think like a scientist: take it apart and look at every piece under a microscope.
words.ex: We had to {analyze} the poem line by line to figure out its meaning.
words.def: to examine something carefully and in detail

words.tip: auto (self) + bio (life) + graphy (writing) = writing about my own life. It usually covers the whole life.
words.ex: In his {autobiography}, the astronaut describes his whole life, from childhood to his last mission.
words.def: the story of a person's own life, written by that person

words.tip: Characters are the cast: WHO is in the story.
words.ex: The main {character} is a girl who finds a secret door in her basement.
words.def: a person in a story, play, or movie

words.tip: con (together) + flict (strike): two sides striking against each other. No conflict, no story!
words.ex: The {conflict} begins when two best friends both want to be team captain.
words.def: a struggle or problem between opposing people or forces in a story

words.tip: DEFY becomes defiance: crossing your arms and saying "No, I won't!"
words.ex: In an act of {defiance}, the students refused to leave until the principal listened.
words.def: open refusal to obey; standing up against authority

words.tip: Determine means to set your mind. Determination is your mind locked on the goal.
words.ex: With pure {determination}, he practiced free throws every day until he made ten in a row.
words.def: the ability to continue trying to do something, although it is very difficult

words.tip: e (out) + DICT (say): an order SAID OUT loud by a king or ruler. Like a dictator's command.
words.ex: The king issued an {edict} that banned music in the village.
words.def: an official order or command given by a person in authority

words.tip: Picture a lightbulb flashing on over your head: "Ohhh, now I get it!"
words.ex: Halfway through the math problem, I had an {epiphany} and the answer suddenly clicked.
words.def: a sudden, clear realization; an "aha!" moment

words.tip: FICtion is FICtional: made up, invented.
words.ex: Dragons and talking cats tell you right away that the book is {fiction}.
words.def: a story that is invented or imagined, not real

words.tip: First person = "I." The narrator is inside the story telling it.
words.ex: The story is told in {first person point of view}: "I opened the door and screamed."
words.def: narration in which the narrator is a character in the story and uses "I"

words.tip: Say ZHAHN-ruh. A genre is like the label on a bookstore shelf: Mystery, Fantasy, Sci-Fi.
words.ex: My favorite {genre} is mystery because I like solving the clues.
words.def: a category or type of literature, such as mystery or fantasy

words.tip: Rights that every HUMAN gets just for being human, everywhere in the world.
words.ex: Freedom of speech and the right to go to school are basic {human rights}.
words.def: the basic rights and freedoms that every person should have

words.tip: Isolate sounds like "isle": put someone alone on an island.
words.ex: The nurse had to {isolate} the sick student so the others wouldn't catch the flu.
words.def: to place or keep someone or something apart from other people or things

words.tip: Memoir sounds like MEMORY. Unlike an autobiography, it focuses on certain memories, not the whole life.
words.ex: Her {memoir} focuses on one summer she spent working on her grandfather's farm.
words.def: a written account of memories from the author's own life experiences

words.tip: The NARRATOR tells the NARRATIVE.
words.ex: His {narrative} about getting lost on the subway made the whole class laugh.
words.def: a story, or an account of connected events

words.tip: NON means not. Not fiction means not made up: it's real.
words.ex: A book that explains how volcanoes erupt is {non-fiction}.
words.def: writing that is based on real facts and real events

words.tip: op + PRESS: being pressed down by unfair power, again and again, for a long time.
words.ex: The people lived under {oppression} for decades, unable to speak freely.
words.def: prolonged cruel, unjust, or unfair treatment or control by an authority

words.tip: perSEVERE: you keep going even when it gets SEVERE.
words.ex: Thanks to her {perseverance}, she finished the marathon after failing twice.
words.def: the continued effort to do or achieve something despite difficulties, failure, or opposition

words.tip: Ask: whose eyes are we looking through?
words.ex: The story feels completely different when told from the dog's {point of view}.
words.def: the position or angle from which a story is told

words.tip: POVerty sounds like POOR.
words.ex: Many families in the story lived in {poverty} and could not afford new shoes.
words.def: the state of being extremely poor; lacking money or resources for basic needs

words.tip: A protocol is the rule book for "how we do things here," like a fire drill plan.
words.ex: Our school's fire drill {protocol} says to line up quietly and leave by the nearest exit.
words.def: the official system of rules, procedures, or proper etiquette

words.tip: pseudo (fake) + nym (name) = fake name. The P is silent: SOO-duh-nim.
words.ex: The author wrote under a {pseudonym} so readers wouldn't know who she really was.
words.def: a fictitious name, especially one used by an author; a pen name

words.tip: Think of a rubber ball: it gets squished, then bounces right back.
words.ex: After losing the first game, the team showed {resilience} and won the next three.
words.def: the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness

words.tip: re + STRICT: a strict limit on what you can do.
words.ex: There is a height {restriction} on that roller coaster, so little kids can't ride.
words.def: a limiting condition or rule that controls what people can or cannot do

words.tip: re + SOLVE. As a verb: decide firmly, or solve the problem. As a noun: firm determination.
words.ex: Their {resolve} never weakened, even when the hike got really tough.
words.def: firm determination or a settled purpose; to decide firmly, or to find a solution

words.tip: Setting = WHERE + WHEN. It sets the stage for the story.
words.ex: The {setting} of the story is a snowy mountain town in the year 1850.
words.def: the place, time, and environment in which a story or event takes place

words.tip: dis (not) + ability: something a body or mind cannot do easily.
words.ex: The school added ramps so students with a {disability} could reach every classroom.
words.def: a physical or mental condition that limits a person's movements, senses, or activities

words.tip: Treating people unfairly just because of the group they belong to.
words.ex: Refusing to hire someone because of their skin color is {discrimination}.
words.def: the unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people

words.tip: Diverse sounds like "different" plus "variety."
words.ex: Our class is {diverse}: students speak eleven different languages at home.
words.def: showing a great deal of variety; very different

words.tip: EM-pathy: putting yourself IN someone else's shoes.
words.ex: Showing {empathy}, he went to sit with the new kid who was eating lunch alone.
words.def: the ability to understand and share the feelings of another

words.tip: Endure: you stay strong until the END.
words.ex: The hikers had to {endure} three hours of freezing rain.
words.def: to suffer (something painful or difficult) patiently

words.tip: A humble person doesn't brag.
words.ex: Even after winning, she stayed {humble} and thanked her teammates.
words.def: having or showing a modest or low estimate of one's importance

words.tip: in + SPIRIT: something breathes energy and ideas into you.
words.ex: The sunset over the river gave her the {inspiration} for her painting.
words.def: the process of being mentally stimulated to do or feel something, especially something creative
